newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-NIGERIAN CUP HOPES GET BOOST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NIGERIAN CUP HOPES GET BOOST.

text.p: Shooting Stars' hopes of becoming the first Nigerian club to win the African Champion's Cup received a boost at the weekend despite a defeat in their quarter-final tie.

Stars lost 1-0 to holders Orlando Pirates of South Africa in the first leg of their tie in Bloemfontein on Sunday but believe the narrow margin can be reversed in the return in Ibadan on September 21.
The match was one of 11 quarter-final, first-leg matches played in the three African club competitions on the weekend.

Pirates scored early, when Dumisa Ngobe converted a 15th minute penalty, but they never looked capable of increasing the margin after that and might not have established a big enough lead for the second leg.
"We are going to have a very tough second game," Pirates captain John Moeti said.
The Nigerians, who have scored eight goals at home in the two previous rounds, celebrated after the first-leg match despite the defeat.
"We will win comfortably in the second leg," predicted international midfielder Sam Pam.
Tunisian club CS Sfaxien recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 5-0 drubbing of Senegal's Diaraf Dakar on Saturday.
Midfielder Skander Souyah began the rout with a second minute goal and the coastal club never looked back after that.
They are likely to be joined in next month's semifinals by Zamalek of Egypt and the Algerian club JS Kabylie.
Zamalek recored a 2-0 home win over COD Meknes of Morocco while Kabylie, with veteran striker Djamel Menad again on the scoresheet, forced a 1-1 draw away at Petro Atletico of Angola.
The African Cup Winners' Cup matches delivered just two goals, both scored by Sodigraf of Zaire in their home win over Nigeria's Katsina United in Kinshasa on Sunday.
Mbayo Kibemba scored shortly after half-time and Kisombe Mundaba added a second in the 66th minute for the 2-0 victory.
Moroccan minnows FUS Rabat were held goalless at home by Arab Contractors of Egypt while a weakened Canon Yaounde suffered the same fate against Costa do Sol of Mozambique in the other games.
FUS Rabat, who play in the second division, could not breach a tough Egyptian defence in front of a paltry 5,000-strong crowd in the Moroccan capital.

Canon, who have won four previous African club titles, had to do without five key players for their home match against the Mozambicans because of an sudden exodus of their leading talent to trials with professional clubs in Europe and Latin America.
In the other Cup Winners' Cup tie, CR Belouizdad of Algeria received a walkover after the withdrawal of South Africa's Pretoria City.
Confederation of African Football (CAF) club holders Etoile Sahel remained on course for a successful defence with a 4-1 crushing of Cameroon's Unisport Bafang in their first leg match.
Imed Ben Younes returned from injury to put the Tunisian team one-up after six minutes and team mates Riadh Delassi, Zoubier Beya and Samir Raouene added three more vital goals.

There was also a comfortable 2-0 win for Mouloudia Oran of Algeria against Vita Club of Zaire on Friday with Cheikh Benzerga and Sabih Ali scoring within minutes on either side of the half-time break.
